_README: Settings of the Kimi (Moonshot AI) portfolio manager (the whole account is managed) - the server profile of the DAILY schedule + crash ladder version, release v3 (2026-09-26) of the ONE-YEAR competition (2026-09-22 .. 2027-09-21 Tehran time). On the server this file is /etc/bitpin-bot/kimi.json (install.sh creates it from this example ONLY if it does not exist; update.sh never changes it; 'sudo python3 deploy/apply_profile.py' updates ONLY the keys of this profile in it, keeps every other value, and makes a backup first). TWO STAGES: stage 1 = the news researcher (section "news", kimi-k2.6 with Moonshot's $web_search) writes a short, sourced news brief ONCE A DAY before the 19:00 decision (fresh for a veto / fill review); stage 2 = the decision model (section "llm", kimi-k3, JSON mode, no tools, no temperature, streamed) decides the allocation ONCE A DAY at 19:00 Tehran plus rare wake-ups, from the live Bitpin market context (the ONLY source of prices and rates), the news brief (untrusted data), docs/STRATEGY_KNOWLEDGE.md and the portfolio. Speed comes from CODE that runs at every hourly check, day and night, without Kimi: the crash-ladder bids, the stops / targets / max holds of every coin position, and the wake-up checks (config.json sections ladder / exits / routing). Kimi has FULL control of the allocation (brain.risk_profile "full"): only the technical guards remain. If the news research fails, stage 2 decides without news; if stage 2 fails, the bot only moves idle toman into USDT_IRT and, after 48 h without a valid decision, its coins too (except coins whose code exits are live). Keys starting with '_' are comments and are ignored; unknown keys are rejected (typo protection). The API key NEVER goes in this file: it goes in /etc/bitpin-bot/bitpin-bot.env as KIMI_API_KEY=... (the same file as the Bitpin keys and KIMI_HTTPS_PROXY); both stages use it. OpenRouter instead of Moonshot: llm.base_url https://openrouter.ai/api/v1, llm.api_key_env OPENROUTER_API_KEY (OPENROUTER_API_KEY=... in the same env file) and an OpenRouter model id; the news section has its own base_url / provider / api_key_env. Any key named like api_key/secret/password in this file is refused. After every edit run: sudo bitpin-bot check (it validates this file exactly as the bot reads it), and then sudo bitpin-bot confirm-live again (the live confirmation covers every value in this file). The drawdown breaker (risk.max_drawdown 0.50 with a rolling 90-day high-water mark, risk.drawdown_action halt) comes from config.json. v3: no default stop on new positions (Kimi sets stop_pct per position, 5..40%), plan horizons 24..720 h, the reply's "analysis" block (p / ev / hurdle / headroom) is checked by code (brain.analysis_policy), the model's reasoning is kept as /var/lib/bitpin-bot/decisions/<time>.reasoning.txt for 60 days. Expected Kimi cost with these settings: about 2-6 USD a month (30 scheduled decisions with the analysis block + 0-8 wake-ups + about 15-38 news calls; the news is reused after a HOLD).

llm._section: bitpin/llm.py LLMClient: stage 2, the DECISION model (OpenAI-compatible chat completions API of Moonshot AI).
llm._base_url: International platform (platform.moonshot.ai). The China platform is https://api.moonshot.cn/v1 - a key only works on the platform that issued it. Must be https; redirects are never followed. OpenRouter: https://openrouter.ai/api/v1 (with provider "auto" and api_key_env OPENROUTER_API_KEY).
llm._provider: The API dialect of base_url: "auto" (recommended) picks it from the host - api.moonshot.ai / api.moonshot.cn = "moonshot", openrouter.ai = "openrouter", any other host = "openai" (a generic OpenAI-compatible API, served like Moonshot). On OpenRouter the reasoning_effort is sent as reasoning.effort ("max" = "high"; "medium" is also accepted there), every reply brings its usage and billed cost (the cost meter records that cost), web search is OpenRouter's web plugin, and HTTP 402 (no credits) raises the same alert as an exhausted Moonshot balance. Set "moonshot", "openrouter" or "openai" only for a relay host that auto cannot recognise; a value that contradicts a known host is refused.
llm._model: Stage 2 decision model: JSON mode, no tools, no temperature (verified on the server 2026-09-22). kimi-k3 cannot use $web_search; the news comes from the "news" section (stage 1). sudo bitpin-bot kimi-check lists the model ids your key can use. On OpenRouter model ids carry the vendor: "moonshotai/kimi-k3" gets the kimi-k3 rules (no temperature, a thinking-size max_tokens), other models (e.g. "openai/gpt-5") get temperature and max_tokens as configured.
llm._api_key_env: Name of the environment variable holding the API key (in /etc/bitpin-bot/bitpin-bot.env). Must be KIMI_* or MOONSHOT_* for Moonshot and OPENROUTER_* (e.g. OPENROUTER_API_KEY) for OpenRouter, so a Bitpin secret can never be sent to an LLM API and a key only goes to the platform that issued it (a mismatch is refused at startup; an OpenRouter key sk-or-... in another platform's variable is not used).
llm._temperature: null = not sent (required for kimi-k3: its JSON mode was verified only WITHOUT temperature).
llm._reasoning_effort: kimi-k3 thinking depth, sent top-level in the request: null = not sent (the API default "max"), "low", "high" or "max". "high" = the owner's cost tier for every call; brain.slot_reasoning_effort can raise the daily slot alone. Never combined with a "thinking" key (refused at startup). On OpenRouter it is sent as reasoning.effort ("max" = "high"; "medium" is also accepted there).
llm._max_tokens: Max completion tokens per request. kimi-k3 is a thinking model: its reasoning tokens count here, and small values give empty replies. Keep 32000.
llm._timeout: HARD limit in seconds of one HTTP request (connect, headers and the whole streamed body; 5..1800); a 32k-token thinking reply can take many minutes (v3.5: 900; a daily decision with reasoning_effort max can take more than 7 minutes). A request that gets no answer at all is ended after 120 s anyway (a dead connection) and retried. Cut to the time left before deadline_seconds.
llm._deadline_seconds: Hard wall-clock limit of one Kimi call including retries (the brain's decision_deadline_seconds can shorten it). 1200 s = one full request (900) + room for a retry after a dropped connection. The bot does nothing else while it waits (the next hourly check waits too).
llm._max_calls_per_day: Hard daily budget of Kimi calls per UTC day (one decision = 1 call, +1 if the reply had to be retried). 24 and not less: a call that fails at once through a dead proxy costs about 0 tokens, and a low cap would lock out the crash calls (review / veto) during an outage; the last brain.reserve_llm_calls of them are kept for review / veto calls. Persisted in /var/lib/bitpin-bot/kimi_budget.json. When exhausted the brain returns an invalid decision: the bot then only runs its fallback. The news researcher has its own budget (news.max_calls_per_day).
llm._max_tokens_per_day: Hard daily budget of tokens (prompt + completion) per UTC day: THE money guard (worst case about 1-4.5 USD a day). A normal day uses one decision of about 10-20k prompt + a few thousand completion tokens. When reached, no new call starts that UTC day. null = no token limit.
llm._max_prompt_tokens_per_call: Only with web search (off for kimi-k3): when one round's prompt grows beyond this, the model must answer. null = no limit.
llm._max_tokens_per_call: Tokens of ONE call over all its rounds together. null = no limit.
llm._max_retries: Retries on HTTP 429 / 5xx / network errors - including 'Remote end closed connection without response' when the Kimi proxy drops the connection, connection resets, incomplete reads, a cut stream and timeouts - with exponential backoff, always inside deadline_seconds. 401/403 fail at once (bad key, wrong platform or region blocked); an exhausted-quota 429 fails at once.
llm._max_timeout_retries: Retries per call of a request that TIMED OUT (Moonshot may already have processed and billed it).
llm._backoff_seconds: First retry wait (3, 6, 12 s ...): a dropped proxy connection usually works again after about 3 s.
llm._max_tool_rounds: Only used with brain.web_search=true (off: kimi-k3 cannot search). Max $web_search rounds per call. Not used on OpenRouter (web search there is one request with its web plugin).
llm._proxy: Keep null. Where Kimi is reached through a local HTTP proxy, set it as KIMI_HTTPS_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:1081 in /etc/bitpin-bot/bitpin-bot.env (it wins over this key and is used by both stages). Only http:// or https:// proxy URLs are accepted. Bitpin traffic never uses a proxy; http_proxy / https_proxy / ALL_PROXY and no_proxy / NO_PROXY are ignored for Kimi. A user:password in the URL is never logged.
llm._stream: true = requests are streamed (stream=true, server-sent events) so bytes keep flowing while kimi-k3 thinks: a proxy tunnel may cut a connection that stays silent for about 2 minutes. If the API refuses streaming (HTTP 400) the bot falls back to normal requests once, logs it and keeps working. Token usage missing from a stream is estimated (never counted as 0). false = never stream (not recommended here).
llm._price_in_per_m: USD per million UNCACHED input tokens of the decision model (kimi-k3 list price 2026-09: 3). Only the cost meter uses the three price_* keys (state_dir/kimi_usage.jsonl -> state_dir/llm_spend.json, the notifier's daily line); they never change what is sent to the API.
llm._price_out_per_m: USD per million output tokens of the decision model, reasoning tokens included (kimi-k3: 15).
llm._price_cached_in_per_m: USD per million CACHED input tokens (Moonshot's automatic prompt cache bills the hit part of a prompt lower; kimi-k3: 0.30). Each request is priced when it is logged, so changing a price never rewrites past spend.

brain._section: bitpin/brain.py KimiBrain: prompt, validation of the model's reply, risk limits, the daily schedule, the wake-ups and the decision modes.
brain._risk_profile: full | conservative | balanced | aggressive (lower case, in quotes). full (the shipped choice: Kimi decides): no per-coin, total-coin, turnover, confidence or IRT-cash cap - only the technical guards remain (strict JSON + allowed-symbol validation, no buying of unavailable / stale / blocked markets, the rebalance threshold and minimum order, the slippage guard, the STOP kill switch, the 30% drawdown breaker, pacing, the decision modes, and the fallback without a valid decision). The others are hard caps: max_coin_weight 0.15/0.30/0.50; max_total_non_usdt 0.30/0.60/1.00; max_turnover 0.30/0.50/0.80; min_confidence 0.60/0.50/0.40; max_irt_cash 0.05.
brain._limits: Optional overrides of the profile numbers, e.g. {"max_coin_weight": 0.25}. Keys: max_coin_weight, max_total_non_usdt, max_turnover (0..2), max_buy_24h (0..2, default = max_turnover), min_confidence, max_irt_cash. An explicit max_turnover / max_buy_24h switches the turnover cap back on, also with "full". Keep {} for full control.
brain._allowed_symbols: The only markets the model may allocate to; each must also be in context.universe. The owner's WIDE universe (decision 2026-09-23: "give it a free hand"): USDT_IRT + 37 coins chosen from a live scan of the top ~70 toman markets by 60-day volume with a spread of at most 0.5% and at least ~5M toman of book depth within 1% of mid on both sides (PAXG / XAUT are gold tokens, SLVON tokenized silver), plus 15 tokenized real-world assets the owner added on 2026-09-26 ("add oil and stocks to the allowed list"): oil USOON, gas UNGON, copper miners COPXON, the US stocks NVDAX / GOOGLX / AAPLX / AMZNX / METAX / COINX / CRCLX / MSFTON / TSMON and the ETFs SPYON / QQQON / TLTON (53 markets; the code blocks buys of the stock / ETF / oil / gas tokens outside US hours or above a 1% spread). Any other symbol in its reply makes the reply invalid. A symbol without fresh market data, with a suspended market or a too wide / empty order book cannot be increased; the slippage guard (1%) and the minimum order protect thin books. Decision.targets always lists every allowed symbol (zeros included) so held coins are sold when the target is 0. The crash ladder uses only ladder_coins (below).
brain._safe_asset: Must be USDT_IRT (the context, prompt and triggers are built around it). Excess above any cap is moved here (never to IRT cash).
brain._decision_times_local: THE SCHEDULE: clock-anchored decision slots, "HH:MM" Tehran time (UTC+03:30, no DST). One scheduled decision a day at 19:00 (the research: anything faster loses money after costs). v3: 19:00 Tehran = 15:30 UTC lies inside the US stock session in US summer and winter time, so the daily decision can buy the tokenized US stocks / ETFs / oil / gas (at the old 13:00 = 09:30 UTC they were always 'us market closed'); crypto trades around the clock. The bot checks at every hourly bar close (HH:01): a slot is due at the first check at or after it when no slot decision ran since. Early decisions (wake-ups, retries) never move the slot. [] = the old elapsed-time schedule (decision_interval_hours, event_move_pct). A second run at 21:00 is NOT recommended (its value is within +-0.3 pp a month).
brain._max_gap_hours: Safety net of the slot schedule: a decision is due when the last one is older than this (24..168).
brain._decision_interval_hours: Only used by the old elapsed-time schedule (decision_times_local []): a decision every N hours.
brain._event_move_pct: Old schedule only: an early decision when a coin moved more than this % since the last decision. With the slot schedule the wake-ups below replace it.
brain._event_min_interval_hours: Early decisions (wake-ups, next_review) happen at most this often after the last decision.
brain._event_scope: Old schedule only: universe = any allowed coin can trigger an early decision; held = only coins held or targeted.
brain._held_move_pct: W3 wake-up (mode held_move): a coin above 1% weight (or a guarded position) moved +-this % in USDT terms since the last decision, crossed one of Kimi's wake levels, or reached its max hold. 12 here since v3 (the owner's one-year Lean cost tier: fewer wake-ups; year review Y3); built-in 8.
brain._drawdown_trigger_points: W4 wake-up: the drawdown from the high-water mark worsened by more than this many points since the last decision -> a RISK_REDUCE call (sell / keep only) when coins are at least risk_reduce_min_coin_weight of equity, otherwise only a notification.
brain._risk_reduce_min_coin_weight: W4: below this coin share of equity the drawdown only notifies (on an all-USDT book the signal is just USDT_IRT falling).
brain._usdt_notify_pct: W5: USDT_IRT moved +-this % in toman since the last decision -> a notification only, no Kimi call (research: switching to toman after such a move loses). null = off.
brain._veto_drop_pct: W2 wake-up (mode VETO, with a fresh news brief): a ladder coin's hourly close fell this % or more below its 48 h high (USDT terms) while its bids rest. Kimi may cancel or shrink THAT coin's bids (hack, delisting, exchange trouble) but may not buy: -15% is not a buy (research: -0.2% at the next close). null = off.
brain._veto_rearm_pct: The veto of a coin re-arms when it is back above -this % from its 48 h high.
brain._ladder_coins: The coins of the crash ladder (resting bids on COIN_USDT; config.json ladder.coins null = this list). The 4 most liquid USDT books. If Bitpin rejects the bids as too small (on a small account they are only a few USDT), use ["BTC", "ETH"] (and config.json ladder.size_frac stays 0.125).
brain._retry_after_invalid_hours: After an invalid decision (LLM error, budget, rejected reply, bad market data) the next attempt waits this long; meanwhile the bot only runs its fallback.
brain._next_review: false (the research spec): the model's next_review_hours is advisory only - the daily slot and the wake-ups decide. true: a value below 24 wakes Kimi for a full, paid decision (an early call, at most max_early_decisions_per_day, never sooner than next_review_min_hours = 6 h): up to 3 extra decisions a day, which the research found no edge for (no cadence under 24 h for routine decisions).
brain._min_decision_spacing_minutes: Pacing: no Kimi call starts less than this many minutes after the previous one (whatever triggered it). A review / veto may still be due one hour later.
brain._max_decisions_per_day: Pacing: at most this many routine Kimi decisions (early ones, retries) in any rolling 24 hours. The daily slot is exempt (it always runs, subject only to the spacing and the LLM budget), and review / veto calls neither count against it nor are blocked by it (they have their own limit: this + reserve_llm_calls). Only decisions where the model answered count, so an outage keeps retrying.
brain._max_early_decisions_per_day: Pacing: at most this many EARLY decisions (wake-ups, next_review) in any rolling 24 hours; review / veto calls are exempt. The scheduled slot always happens.
brain._reserve_llm_calls: Kept for review / veto calls (the ladder): the last N calls of llm.max_calls_per_day and the last N x one call's tokens (llm.max_tokens + ~12k prompt) of llm.max_tokens_per_day (each at most half of the limit). Other calls - the slot, early calls, retries - stop there, counting their OWN worst case too (1 + max_validation_retries calls of that size): a routine decision may start only if the reserve is still whole after it.
brain._early_search_budget_fraction: Only with web_search (off): when this share of today's llm.max_tokens_per_day is used, early decisions run without web search.
brain._decision_ttl_minutes: A decision expires this long after it was made; the bot never executes an expired decision.
brain._fallback: What the bot does WITHOUT a valid Kimi decision (Kimi unreachable, the proxy down, invalid replies, budget used up; it never trades otherwise). Cash sweep (always on): toman above sweep_irt_above (0.05 = 5% of equity) is moved into USDT_IRT, coins untouched - except that the toman share of the last VALID Kimi decision is kept while that decision is younger than derisk_after_hours. derisk_after_hours 48 (the research; with one decision a day this still needs at least 2 failed slots - a 12 h derisk would dump a crash buy during a proxy outage): after this long without a valid decision every coin is sold into USDT_IRT, EXCEPT coins whose code exits are live (they are left to their stop / target); null disables it. Both skip the turnover cap but keep every other safety check of the bot.
brain._endgame: The competition endgame (Tehran times; v3: the ONE-YEAR competition ends 2027-09-21T20:30Z = 2027-09-22 00:00 Tehran, so the cut-off is 2027-09-16 13:00 and the FINAL decision 2027-09-20 13:00; the bot warns at startup when these dates and context.competition_end_utc are more than 14 days apart). From no_new_entries_at: every crash-ladder bid is cancelled and no coin may be bought (every mode). max_hold_cap_at: no max hold runs past it. The first scheduled decision at or after final_at is the FINAL one: Kimi states the end state; a coin stays only if Kimi keeps it explicitly; the default for coins is USDT_IRT, never toman. default_to_usdt_after_hours: without a valid final decision this long after final_at the bot moves every coin into USDT_IRT itself. end_at null = context.competition_end_utc; after it every endgame flag is off (owner mode). null for the whole object switches the endgame off.
brain._web_search: Keep false: kimi-k3 cannot use Moonshot's $web_search (HTTP 400 'tokenization failed'; true is refused at startup). The news comes from the "news" section (stage 1).
brain._json_mode: Send response_format {type: json_object} (verified with kimi-k3); the reply must then be exactly one JSON object.
brain._max_validation_retries: If the reply fails validation, ask again once with the error message (if the decision deadline allows); still invalid -> Decision(valid=False), no trade.
brain._sum_tolerance: targets + cash_irt must be within 1 +/- this; within it the weights are normalised, outside it the reply is invalid.
brain._recent_decisions: How many of the brain's own previous valid decisions are shown to the model.
brain._fees: Shown to the model (fractions: 0.003 = 0.30%; verified live for COIN_IRT and COIN_USDT markets).
brain._rebalance_threshold: Weight changes smaller than this are not executed. The bot uses config.json's rebalance_threshold when it builds the brain, and raises the step to one minimum order when that is larger.
brain._decision_deadline_seconds: Hard wall-clock limit of one whole decision (the Kimi call plus the validation retry): 1500 s = one llm.deadline_seconds call (1200) + a retry. The STOP kill-switch file is checked before every Kimi request.
brain.extra_instructions: OWNER'S STYLE: AGGRESSIVE. The owner wants the maximum account value in toman at the end of the one-year competition and accepts large drawdowns on the way. Aggressive means: a candidate that passes THE HURDLE may be sized up to the headroom - size it boldly, concentration in one or two coins and a large coin share are allowed. It does not mean a lower hurdle: the research numbers are facts, a failing candidate gets 0, and USDT_IRT is where the money sits whenever nothing passes - the null hypothesis, not caution. Do not stay in USDT out of caution alone when a candidate passes; never churn (a round trip costs about 1.8-2.4% through the toman markets, 0.8-1.1% through BTC/ETH/XRP/SOL_USDT); keep the account away from the drawdown halt (config.json risk.max_drawdown: a halt freezes the account for the rest of the year). Never buy a coin because it just spiked. ASSET CLASSES (2026-09-26): besides coins the universe carries tokenized gold (PAXG, XAUT, GLDON), silver (SLVON), oil (USOON), gas (UNGON), copper (COPXON), US stocks (xStocks ...X, Ondo ...ON, bStocks ...B) and US ETFs (SPYON, QQQON, TLTON, AGGON, IEFAON, SMHB, DRAMB); COINX, CRCLX, MSTRON and HOODX are crypto beta, not diversification. Judge them by the UNDERLYING (its outlook, its news), never by the token's own hourly moves: the tokens track the reference with 2-3% quote noise and stale weekend prints, so a stock or oil token is a view of at least 30 days, never a swing trade; buy them only while the US session is open (the code refuses the buy when it is closed or the spread is wide) and give them no tight stop (a -12% stop on the hourly close fired in 6-11% of weeks from quote noise alone). Gold (XAUT first: the tightest book) is a legitimate alternative to the USDT sleeve when its base-rate row supports it, not a hedge to hold out of fear.
brain._extra_instructions: Appended to the system prompt as the owner's own guidance: the owner's AGGRESSIVE style (bitpin/brain.py AGGRESSIVE_STYLE_INSTRUCTIONS, v3: aggressive = full sizing of a candidate that passes THE HURDLE, never a lower hurdle; USDT_IRT is the null hypothesis, not caution) plus the ASSET CLASSES note of 2026-09-26 (gold / silver / oil / gas / copper / US stock and ETF tokens: judged by the underlying, bought only while the US session is open, no tight stop; COINX / CRCLX / MSTRON / HOODX are crypto beta). Max 4000 characters. "" = none.
brain._log_full_context: Also store the full market context and the news text in every kimi_decisions.jsonl line (about 15-25 kB per decision, ~1 MB a month; the digest and key numbers are always stored). true since v3: replaying a live decision needs the exact messages it saw.
brain._analysis_policy: v3: the code check of the reply's "analysis" block (bitpin/brain.py parse_analysis: a coin whose weight rises needs a candidate with pass true, a row that covers the plan's horizon, cost_pct at least the route floor, loss_pct / gain_pct that match the plan's levels, p0 = l / (g + l), p at most min(0.80, p0 + 0.20), ev_pct recomputed, pass = ev_pct >= 0, verdicts that match the weight change, scenario_loss_pct within the headroom to the halt, cited field=value that match the context). "off" = the problems are logged as adjustment notes only (the first live week: read before enforcing); "block" = a failing reply is sent back once, then the failing coin's INCREASE is blocked (never a forced sale, never a lost decision); "error" = rejected on every attempt (the last allocation persists).
brain._slot_reasoning_effort: v3: the kimi-k3 reasoning effort of the daily slot decision only (null = llm.reasoning_effort; "low", "high" or "max"): "max" lets the daily decision think at full depth while the wake-ups keep the cheaper client value.
brain._require_plan: ENTRY PLANS (true, the default; also when this key is missing): every NEW coin position Kimi opens needs its plan in the reply - setup (dip_in_uptrend, trend_continuation, breakout, crash_rebound, relative_strength, mean_reversion, macro_hedge, other), horizon_hours 24..720 (a day to 30 days), invalidation_usdt (the USDT price below which an hourly close proves the thesis wrong), optionally take_profit_usdt and a note of at most 160 characters. The bot keeps the plan with the position (runner state) and shows it back to Kimi in every later decision as ITS OWN earlier plan (the note is sanitised: plain words only, links / mentions / instructions removed), with the rule: no exit or reversal before the horizon unless the invalidation broke, the stop / target fired or Kimi names NEW information. An hourly close below the invalidation level wakes Kimi (HELD_MOVE); nothing is sold by it. A reply that opens a position without a plan is sent back once; then that coin is not bought (the rest of the decision stands). false = plans optional (still recorded and shown back when given).

context._section: bitpin/analysis.py MarketContextBuilder: what the model sees (public Bitpin data + your portfolio snapshot).
context._universe: Markets analysed per symbol (must contain every brain.allowed_symbols entry). With more than compact_symbols_above of them, only USDT_IRT, the ladder coins and the held / targeted / focused coins get full detail; every other coin is one compact row.
context._macro_symbols: Extra markets always fetched for the macro section (USDT_IRT = toman devaluation, PAXG_IRT = gold).
context._competition_start_utc: 2026-09-22 00:00 Tehran (the ONE-YEAR competition runs 2026-09-22 .. 2027-09-21 Tehran time). Used for days elapsed and the hold-USDT benchmark since the start. Correct it if the official rules give another time.
context._competition_end_utc: 2027-09-22 00:00 Tehran = the end of 2027-09-21 Tehran time (the last day of the one-year competition; brain.endgame is set 1-5 days before it and the bot warns when the two disagree by more than 14 days). Correct it if the official rules give another time. Accepted forms: "2027-09-21T20:30:00Z" (UTC), "2027-09-22T00:00:00+03:30" or "2027-09-22 00:00 Tehran" (Tehran time). A wrong format stops the bot at startup with a clear message.
context._equity_start_irt: Account value in toman at the competition start (for P&L %), e.g. 5000000. null = the first equity seen, persisted in /var/lib/bitpin-bot/kimi_equity.json.
context._irt_asset: Wallet code of toman cash in the balances snapshot. The bot passes its broker balances with toman under IRT (already divided by config.json irt_unit_divisor), so keep IRT. A toman/rial-looking balance under any other code makes the brain refuse to decide (the weights would be wrong).
context._irt_unit_divisor: Only for raw wallet balances: 10 if the irt_asset amount is in rial. Keep 1 with the bot (config.json irt_unit_divisor is applied before).
context._lookback_bars: Hourly candles kept per symbol when rule_signals is on (same as the runner, so the strategies see the same history). Later builds download only new candles.
context._analysis_lookback_bars: Hourly candles when rule_signals is off (enough for 30-day returns and EMA200 on 4h).
context._orderbook: Fetch each symbol's order book (spread, depth within 1%/2% of mid).
context._matches: v3: ignored (the order-flow block of the context was removed; true is accepted with a startup warning and fetches nothing). Keep false.
context._market_status: Fetch Bitpin's market list (one public request) and block increases of markets marked not tradable or suspended.
context._max_spread_pct: A coin whose order book is empty, one-sided or has a wider spread than this (in %) is marked 'blocked' in the context and cannot be increased (it can still be sold).
context._build_time_budget_seconds: Max seconds to collect the market data of one decision; after that no further request starts, the remaining symbols are marked unavailable (and cannot be increased). Keeps a slow or throttled Bitpin API from blocking the bot.
context._rule_signals: v3 default false: the rule-based strategies of bitpin/strategies are not shown (only hold_usdt passed the holdout; the block cost 1-2k characters of prompt for weak evidence). true = show their current target weights with the holdout verdict.
context._rule_strategies: null = every discovered strategy; or a list of names, e.g. ["hold_usdt", "trend_donchian"].
context._rule_params: Optional parameters per strategy, e.g. {"trend_donchian": {"entry_n": 240}}; default_params otherwise.
context._verified_strategies: Strategies that passed the unseen 150-day holdout (only hold_usdt did). All others are labelled as rejected.
context._rule_time_budget_seconds: Strategies not started within this time are skipped (listed in the context).
context._recent_decisions: Max previous decisions included in the context.
context._max_context_chars: Size guard (~9k tokens; v3 default 26000, the 53-symbol universe with compact rows is about 21k): if the JSON is larger, rule descriptions, the beta / correlation fields, order books and the adjustment notes are dropped step by step.
context._compact_symbols_above: A universe larger than this is shown COMPACT (full detail for USDT_IRT, BTC, ETH, XRP, SOL and every held / guarded / targeted / focused coin; one row with price, USDT returns 24h/7d/30d, RSI 4h, distance from the 48 h high, live spread and 1% depth for the others): the 38-symbol universe then fits in about 10k characters. 0 = full detail for every symbol.

news._section: bitpin/news.py NewsResearcher. research() never raises: when the news cannot be fetched the decision is made without news (or with the last good brief, marked STALE) and the prompt says so.
news._enabled: false = no news research at all; stage 2 is told that no news is available.
news._base_url: OpenAI-compatible endpoint: Moonshot, or OpenRouter at https://openrouter.ai/api/v1 (see provider). Must be https; redirects are never followed. When the bot builds the researcher from kimi.json and this key is absent, llm.base_url (with llm.provider) is used.
news._provider: The API dialect of base_url: "auto" (recommended) picks it from the host - api.moonshot.ai / api.moonshot.cn = "moonshot" (Moonshot's builtin $web_search tool loop), openrouter.ai = "openrouter", any other host = "openai" (a generic OpenAI-compatible API, served like Moonshot). On OpenRouter the research is ONE request with OpenRouter's web search plugin (max_results = min(10, 2 x max_items); OpenRouter bills the search results unless the model searches natively) instead of the $web_search tool loop, so max_tool_rounds and max_prompt_tokens_per_call are not used there; the usage and the cost OpenRouter reports are what the cost meter records, and HTTP 402 (no credits) raises the same alert as an exhausted Moonshot balance. Set "moonshot", "openrouter" or "openai" only for a relay host that auto cannot recognise; a value that contradicts a known host is refused. When the bot builds the researcher from kimi.json and neither this key nor base_url is set, llm.provider is used.
news._api_key_env: Name of the environment variable holding the key of the news API (in /etc/bitpin-bot/bitpin-bot.env; the key itself never goes in this file): KIMI_* or MOONSHOT_* for Moonshot, OPENROUTER_* (e.g. OPENROUTER_API_KEY) for OpenRouter - a key is only ever sent to the platform that issued it (a mismatch is refused at startup), and an OpenRouter key (sk-or-...) found in the variable of another platform is not used. When the bot builds the researcher from kimi.json and this key is absent: llm.api_key_env when the news runs on the llm's own non-Moonshot platform (e.g. both on OpenRouter), else KIMI_API_KEY (on Moonshot a custom KIMI_* / MOONSHOT_* variable of llm is used, as before).
news._model: Stage-1 model. Must support Moonshot's builtin $web_search tool: verified for kimi-k2.6; kimi-k3 does NOT work (HTTP 400 'tokenization failed' when the search result is echoed back). On OpenRouter the web plugin searches for the model, so any model id of its list works (the ids carry the vendor: "vendor/model").
news._max_tokens: Max completion tokens per request (256..262144). kimi-k2.6 reasons before answering: with small values (e.g. 50) it spends everything on reasoning and returns an empty reply. Keep >= 16000 (v3.5: 8000 cut a reply short; a reply cut off anyway keeps its complete items, or is asked for once more).
news._temperature: null = not sent (the model's default; recommended). A number 0..2 is sent as is.
news._proxy: Kimi traffic only. The environment variable KIMI_HTTPS_PROXY (e.g. http://127.0.0.1:1081 in /etc/bitpin-bot/bitpin-bot.env) wins over this key; without either, and without llm.proxy when built from kimi.json, requests go DIRECT. Only http:// or https:// proxy URLs (host and port). A configured proxy is ALWAYS used: http_proxy / https_proxy / ALL_PROXY, no_proxy / NO_PROXY and the Windows proxy settings are never consulted. A user:password in the URL is never logged.
news._timeout: HARD wall-clock limit in seconds of one HTTP request (connect, headers and the whole streamed body), cut to the time left before deadline_seconds. 300 s measured as enough on the server.
news._deadline_seconds: Hard wall-clock limit of one research call: all search rounds, retries and waits (20..1800). When reached the call fails and the decision is made with the last good brief (see max_stale_minutes) or without news. The STOP kill switch also ends a running call before its next request.
news._max_retries: Retries of one request after a network drop (RemoteDisconnected 'Remote end closed connection without response' when the Kimi proxy drops the connection, connection reset, incomplete read, timeout, URLError), HTTP 429 (not for an exhausted quota) or 5xx, with exponential backoff. HTTP 400/401/403 are never retried.
news._backoff_seconds: First retry wait (doubles each retry: 3, 6, 12 s ...). A retry after ~3 s usually succeeds through the Kimi proxy.
news._backoff_max_seconds: Upper bound of one retry wait.
news._max_tool_rounds: Max $web_search rounds (1..10; the model may run several searches in one round); after that the tool is withdrawn and the model must answer with what it has found. Every round re-sends ALL earlier search results (one result is about 5-7k tokens), so the prompt grows with each round: 3 rounds cost roughly 20-50k tokens per research call. Not used on OpenRouter (one request with the web search plugin).
news._max_prompt_tokens_per_call: When one request's prompt is larger than this (prompt_tokens reported by the API), no more searches are allowed and the model must answer now (2000..1000000, null = no cap).
news._max_tokens_per_day: Hard daily token budget of all research calls per UTC day (10000..100000000, null = no cap), persisted in state_dir/news_budget.json. When it is reached no new research call starts (the last good brief is used while younger than max_stale_minutes), and a running call gets no more searches. This is on top of stage 2's own llm.max_tokens_per_day.
news._cache_minutes: A brief younger than this is reused without a new call (state_dir/news_cache.json): 1380 min = 23 h, so the news is researched ONCE A DAY, right before the 19:00 decision. A veto or a ladder-fill review forces a fresh brief (focused on that coin). 0 = a new call for every decision.
news._after_hold_only: true = after a decision that was a plain HOLD, the daily brief is researched again only when the cached brief is older than 48 hours (a wake-up / veto / fill review always researches); the last good brief is reused meanwhile. A HOLD means the model saw nothing to act on, so yesterday's brief plus the live market context is enough for the next look (about 0.6 research calls a day instead of 1). false = research whenever the brief is older than cache_minutes, as before.
news._max_stale_minutes: When a refresh fails, a daily budget is used up or the key is missing, the last good brief is still used (marked STALE in the prompt, with its time) while it is younger than this: 1440 = the brief of the previous daily run. 0 = never use a stale brief.
news._retry_after_failure_minutes: After a failed research call no new attempt starts for this long (the stale brief or 'no news' is used meanwhile). A call ended by the kill switch does not start this pause.
news._max_calls_per_day: Hard daily budget of research calls per UTC day (one call = all its search rounds), persisted in state_dir/news_budget.json. v3: 2 = the daily run (reused after a HOLD, see after_hold_only) plus one forced brief (a veto or a ladder-fill review); a third wake-up the same day decides with the last good brief (max_stale_minutes). Failed calls count. 0 = never call.
news._max_items: Max news items kept in the brief (1..20).
news._max_chars: Max characters of the rendered brief given to the decision model (300..8000); items that do not fit are left out. Every item is sanitised: Unicode-normalised, control characters stripped, fields truncated, price / rate / amount figures replaced by '[number removed]' (dates, percentages kept), source URLs reduced to scheme://host; items that read like instructions to the reader, claim that the Bitpin data is wrong, or are not in English are dropped, and the brief says how many were removed.
news.extra_topics: oil prices, OPEC and Middle East supply; gold, Fed policy and real yields; US stock market, Nvidia/AI and big-tech earnings; Iran oil exports and sanctions
news._extra_topics: Optional extra topics for the researcher (max 1000 characters), e.g. "Bitpin trading competition rule changes". Never put instructions for the decision model here.
news._sources: v3.5: the trusted news sites (domains; subdomains count; at most 100): international agencies and business media, crypto media, Iranian economic and news media, official sources. The researcher searches and cites only these; an item whose article is on any other site (or has no source) is left out, and the researcher's summary with it (it may rest on that item). This list is the built-in default (bitpin/news.py DEFAULT_NEWS_SOURCES): null or a missing key = the same list. The panel's Trade settings -> News edits it; [] = any site (not recommended).
news._stream: true = requests are streamed (stream=true, server-sent events) so bytes keep flowing while the model thinks; the tunnel drops connections that stay silent for about 2 minutes. If the API refuses streaming (HTTP 400) the bot falls back to normal requests once, logs it and keeps working. Token usage missing from a stream is estimated (never counted as 0). false = never stream.
news._price_in_per_m: USD per million uncached input tokens of the news model (kimi-k2.6 list price 2026-09: about 1). Only the LLM cost meter uses the three price_* keys (state_dir/news_usage.jsonl -> state_dir/llm_spend.json, shown in the Telegram daily line); they never change what is sent to the API.
news._price_out_per_m: USD per million output tokens of the news model, reasoning included (kimi-k2.6: 4).
news._price_cached_in_per_m: USD per million cached input tokens (Moonshot's automatic prompt cache; kimi-k2.6: 0.16). Each request is priced when it is logged, so changing a price never rewrites past spend.

guard._section: bitpin/analysis.py pump_guard + bitpin/brain.py: the ANTI-PUMP BUY GUARD (on by default, also when this section is missing). The pump study of 2026-09-23 (all 547 Bitpin IRT markets, 400 days, 1031 pumps): buying AFTER a coin pumped 30%+ lost money in every month studied (24 h later -6% on average, 7 days later -13% median, only 25-30% ended higher; 5-8% round trip on the thin books). So the code never BUYS (new or larger weight) a coin whose USDT-terms hourly close rose pump_rise_pct or more above its close pump_window_hours earlier (point to point, as in the study: a V-shaped rebound from a crash that is not 30% above where the coin was 24 h before is NOT a pump), within the last pump_lookback_hours - until pump_lookback_hours after that pump. Selling is always allowed. The context marks such coins "pump_guard": "until <Tehran time>"; a decision that still targets more weight is cut back to the current weight (the rest to USDT_IRT) with a note, and the runner re-checks its own candles before it executes (a clamp there is a decision note and a Telegram message). The CRASH LADDER is covered too: while a ladder coin is guarded its resting ladder bids are cancelled, none is placed or re-armed, and a decision may not raise its ladder scale; its bids follow the scale again when the guard ends. Applies to every coin except USDT_IRT (gold / silver tokens included).
guard._pump_rise_pct: The rise (in %, USDT terms) that counts as a pump (5..1000). null = the guard is OFF (not recommended).
guard._pump_window_hours: Within how many hours the rise must happen (1..168).
guard._pump_lookback_hours: How long a pump blocks buying (1..720): pumps that closed within the last N hours count, and the coin is buyable again N hours after the latest one.
